challenges.claim: observed_substrate_signal #3 calls web:Ps.68.5 ("is God in his holy habitation") "Participial predication," but the MT verse behind it (oshb:Ps.68.6) is a bare nominal/construct-noun clause with no verb at all — there is no participle there. The genuine Hiphil participles that would substantiate a participial-mood claim occur one verse later, at oshb:Ps.68.7 (=web:Ps.68.6), which is inside this row's own span but is not the verse the claim cites.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.68.6 (byte, collate.py GREEN): אֲבִ֣י יְ֭תוֹמִים וְדַיַּ֣ן אַלְמָנ֑וֹת אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים בִּמְע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ — no verb (אֲבִי "father of" and וְדַיַּן "and judge of" are construct-state agent nouns, not participles). Contrast oshb:Ps.68.7 (byte): אֱלֹהִ֤ים מ֘וֹשִׁ֤יב יְחִידִ֨ים בַּ֗יְתָה מוֹצִ֣יא אֲ֭סִירִים בַּכּוֹשָׁר֑וֹת אַ֥ךְ ס֝וֹרֲרִ֗ים שָׁכְנ֥וּ צְחִיחָֽה — מוֹשִיב/מוֹצִיא are genuine Hiphil participles ("the one who settles" / "the one who brings out"). WEB “A father of the fatherless, and a defender of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.” (web:Ps.68.5) supplies the copula "is," which has no Hebrew counterpart at that verse.

challenges.claim: The rationale's "triple imperative" label for web:Ps.68.1 mislabels three 3rd-person volitive imperfects (jussive force, English "Let...") as grammatical imperatives. A true Hebrew imperative is a distinct 2nd-person form, exemplified later in the same rationale at web:Ps.68.4/oshb:Ps.68.5 (שִׁ֤ירוּ "sing!").
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.68.2 (=web:Ps.68.1, byte): יָק֣וּם אֱ֭לֹהִים יָפ֣וּצוּ אוֹיְבָ֑יו וְיָנ֥וּסוּ מְ֝שַׂנְאָ֗יו מִפָּנָֽיו — יָקוּם/יָפוּצוּ/וְיָנוּסוּ are 3rd-person (ms/mp) imperfects carrying jussive force ("let him arise / let them be scattered / let them flee"), not 2nd-person imperative morphology.

I independently tested the row's own rejected-alternative logic by looking for a rival seam the row did not consider: oshb:Ps.68.10-11 (=web:68.9-10, "You, God, sent a plentiful rain. You confirmed your inheritance when it was weary. Your congregation lived therein. You, God, prepared your goodness for the poor.") is genuine 2nd-singular direct address to God (confirmed 2ms suffixes/perfect in גֶּ֣שֶׁם נְ֭דָבוֹת תָּנִ֣יף אֱלֹהִ֑ים נַחֲלָתְךָ֥ וְ֝נִלְאָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה כֽוֹנַנְתָּֽהּ / חַיָּתְךָ֥ יָֽשְׁבוּ בָ֑הּ תָּ֤כִ֥ין בְּטוֹבָתְךָ֖ לֶעָנִ֣י אֱלֹהִֽים), embedded between 3rd-person theophany narration at oshb:Ps.68.9 (אֶ֤רֶץ רָעָ֨שָׁה אַף שָׁמַ֣יִם נָטְפוּ֮ מִפְּנֵ֪י אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים זֶ֥ה סִינַ֑י מִפְּנֵ֥י אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) and 3rd-person "the Lord announced" at oshb:Ps.68.12 (אֲדֹנָ֥י יִתֶּן אֹ֑מֶר הַֽ֝מְבַשְּׂר֗וֹת צָבָ֥א רָֽב). This is a real person-shift, but it does not amount to a fresh addressee: the row's own opening verse, oshb:Ps.68.8 (=web:68.7, "in your going out... your people... your marching"), already establishes 2nd-singular address to God, so the alternation is a return to that same sustained addressee, not the introduction of a new one — a well-attested feature of Hebrew hymnic style that is not by itself a segmentation signal. The rejected_alternative (testing only a split at web:68.11, where the text stays 3rd-person with no addressee change) stands. One imprecision noted but not filed as a formal challenge here: the rationale's "the scene shift to direct address of the Bashan mountains at web:Ps.68.15" mischaracterizes oshb:Ps.68.16 (=web:68.15), a verbless 3rd-person naming chain with no vocative; the actual 2nd-person-plural vocative (תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮, "why do you leap enviously") first appears at oshb:Ps.68.17 (=web:68.16). This does not affect this row's own span, whose boundary rests on the Selah-marked opening at 68:7 and the topic shift at 68:15 (still valid regardless of grammatical person) — see M8-Ps-192, whose own opening warrant this same issue affects materially.

All quoted WEB spans (68:15, 68:16, 68:17, 68:18) are byte-exact against verse_map_web.json; boundary_evidence_refs correctly includes 68:7 and 68:14 even though they sit outside this row's own span, since they are argued in prose. The strophe's overall content grouping (mountain rivalry, chariot procession, ascent) is not in dispute. But the row's central tier-1 warrant misidentifies which verse actually carries the vocative that is supposed to open the strophe.

challenges.claim: The rationale calls web:Ps.68.15 ("The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged.") both "Direct address" and "a tier-1 vocative-shift opener," but the underlying MT verse (oshb:Ps.68.16) is a verbless, 3rd-person construct-noun chain with no vocative or 2nd-person form of any kind. The actual 2nd-person-plural vocative to the mountains occurs one verse later, at oshb:Ps.68.17 (=web:Ps.68.16) — which the row's own rejected_alternative paragraph correctly identifies ("the second-person vocative to 'you rugged mountains' (web:Ps.68.16)"), directly contradicting the rationale's claim two paragraphs earlier that web:Ps.68.15 is where the vocative shift happens. The row is internally inconsistent about its own primary boundary signal.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.68.16 (=web:Ps.68.15, byte, collate.py GREEN): הַר אֱ֭לֹהִים הַר בָּשָׁ֑ן הַ֥ר גַּ֝בְנֻנִּ֗ים הַר בָּשָֽׁן — no verb, no 2nd-person form. oshb:Ps.68.17 (=web:Ps.68.16, byte): לָ֤מָּה תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮ הָרִ֪ים גַּבְנֻ֫נִּ֥ים הָהָ֗ר חָמַ֣ד אֱלֹהִ֣ים לְשִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אַף יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָנֶֽצַח — תְּֽרַצְּדוּן֮ is the 2mp imperfect (paragogic nun) carrying the direct address ("why do you [pl] leap enviously"). WEB confirms the same divide in English: “The mountains of Bashan are majestic mountains. The mountains of Bashan are rugged.” (web:Ps.68.15, 3rd-person) versus “Why do you look in envy, you rugged mountains, at the mountain where God chooses to reign?” (web:Ps.68.16, 2nd-person). Note: since oshb:Ps.68.17 is still inside this row's own span (68.15-68.18), the span choice itself is not necessarily wrong — only the stated warrant for where the tier-1 signal sits.

challenges.claim: Both the rationale and observed_substrate_signal #2 state that WEB renders MT's אֱלֹהִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.68.27) as "the Lord" at web:Ps.68.26. This identifies the wrong Hebrew word. MT oshb:Ps.68.27 contains BOTH אֱלֹהִ֑ים and יְ֝הוָ֗ה as separate terms; WEB renders אֱלֹהִ֑ים as "God" (its ordinary, unremarkable convention throughout the psalm) and renders יְ֝הוָ֗ה — not אֱלֹהִ֑ים — as "the Lord." This is precisely the toolkit-flagged, Phase-0-verified hazard at this verse ("Ps 68:26 (WEB) = 68:27 (MT): WEB renders YHWH as 'the Lord' here"), and the row inverts it, misattributing the substituted rendering to the wrong divine name.
challenges.evidence: oshb:Ps.68.27 (=web:Ps.68.26, byte, collate.py GREEN): בְּֽ֭מַקְהֵלוֹת בָּרְכ֣וּ אֱלֹהִ֑ים יְ֝הוָ֗ה מִמְּק֥וֹר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — אֱלֹהִ֑ים appears first (WEB: "God"), יְ֝הוָ֗ה appears second (WEB: "the Lord"). WEB: ““Bless God in the congregations, even the Lord in the assembly of Israel!”” (web:Ps.68.26) — "God" tracks אֱלֹהִ֑ים, "the Lord" tracks יְ֝הוָ֗ה, not אֱלֹהִ֑ים as the row states.
